newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts Banca di Roma individual rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts Banca di Roma individual rating.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Wednesday it affirmed the long- and short-term ratings on Banca di Roma but cut the Italian bank's individual rating to C/D from C. The legal rating remains unchanged at 2, it said.
"The ratings reflect BdR's strong domestic competitive position, in particular in the central regions of the country," IBCA said in a statement.

"Profitability, however, remains depressed as the bank is still dealing with a high cost structure inherited from the merger and with a relative deterioration in its asset quality indicators. As a result we expect loan loss provisions to remain high in the near future," it said.

"Nevertheless, pre-provisioning profitability is increasing in 1996 as the group is reducing personnel and controlling costs more efficiently. Lending and funding volumes are also increasing with a positive impact on interest rate revenue," the IBCA statement said.
Legal ratings deal with the question of whether an institution would receive support either from owners or governmental authorities if it ran into difficulties, IBCA said.

"While we consider the legal rating to be a prime factor in the assessment of credit risk, IBCA's individual ratings permit an evaluation divorced entirely from any consideration of outside support," the agency said.
